Pushed as Gerrit change 1938 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1938), commit 59bae00079.

CONCERN BOUNDARY: tracker provisioning vs. tickets-branch convergence.
init.py held two subsystems the call graph already separates. The `init` command proper
(`init_cli` -> `init_core` -> `_mount_or_create_branch` / `_init_via_symlink`, plus the
`pending_init_*` predicates) never calls the ensure units; their sole caller is
`_store/ensures._registry()`, which lazy-imports and dispatches them by id. Serena's
reference search over all five units returns exactly that one call site. `ensures.py`'s own
docstring already recorded the seam: the units lived in init only because they owned the
`.gitignore`/`.gitattributes` templates.

MOVED to `src/rebar/_commands/_init_ensures.py` (237 LOC), byte-identical (AST-verified):
`_GITIGNORE`, `_GITATTRIBUTES`, `_gc_config_unit`, `_merge_ours_unit`, `_gitattributes_unit`,
`_gitignore_unit`, `_store_compat_unit`.

SIZES: init.py 786 -> 610 LOC (190 lines of headroom under the 800 cap; clear of the gate's
own 720 near-cap band). New module 237 LOC. Neither is under the 100-LOC floor.

KEPT IN PLACE: `_untrack_runtime_markers_unit` + `_UNTRACK_BATCH`. It is not a content
converger (no template; it repairs a legacy index with `git rm --cached`), AND
tests/unit/test_ensures_untrack_markers.py:155 does
`monkeypatch.setattr(init_mod, "_UNTRACK_BATCH", 3)`. Splitting the unit from the constant
would have left that patch silently inert - the test would still pass while no longer
exercising the multi-batch path. That is the "keep the half tests bind to" rule.

BINDING CHECK, BOTH SIDES:
- What patches what I MOVED: nothing monkeypatches the five moved units or the two templates.
  `ensures._registry()` reaches them as module ATTRIBUTES of `init` and
  tests/interfaces/store/test_ensure_drift_matrix.py:25 does
  `from rebar._commands.init import _GITIGNORE` - both preserved by re-exporting the moved
  names from init.py, so `_registry()` needed no change.
- What patches what my MOVED CODE CALLS: the moved units call only `_git` (now a local
  wrapper over the shared `_store.gitutil.run_git_write` seam) and, lazily,
  `compat.write_compat_record`. Nothing in the tree patches `run_git_write` or
  `init.run_git_write`. Verified no test patches `init._git` on any path reaching a moved
  unit: test_init_attach_predicate.py patches `init._git` but also spies out `init.init_core`,
  so no sweep runs; the ensure suites patch only env vars, `ensures.write_lock` and
  `ensures._registry`.
- Monkeypatches pinned to `init` (`run_git`, `_git`, `_git_ok`, `_git_fetch`,
  `_ensure_branch_user_config`, `init_core`, `_UNTRACK_BATCH`) all target symbols that stay.

PATH-KEYED REGISTRIES:
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` - its only init.py key is `_mount_or_create_branch` (18),
  which stays; `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` run DIRECTLY reports
  `active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.
- `tests/scripts/test_cli_seam_clean_heldout.py` `_OWNED_FILES` / `_MARKER_BUDGET` - init.py's
  read-via marker budget is ZERO and the moved cluster contained no `# read-via:` line, so the
  budget did not constrain the seam (checked before committing to it, per the executor.py
  lesson). `check_config_ownership.py` exits 0.
- `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` - the moved `_git` wrapper carries its `# raw-git-ok:`
  reason; gate exits 0.
- `docs/cli-reference.md` IS generated ("do not edit by hand") and CI drift-gated. Regenerated
  with `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`: byte-identical, because no CLI surface moved
  (`init_cli` / `init_core` untouched). No file change, so nothing to add to file_impact.
- `docs/architecture.md`'s three `_commands.init` citations all name symbols that stay.
- `.github/module-size-limit.txt` byte-identical to origin/main.

VALIDATION ACROSS THE WHOLE TREE (not just tests/unit): `pytest -m "not integration and not
external"` over tests/unit + tests/interfaces + tests/scripts + tests/e2e =
14508 passed, 63 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failed (18:59). `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
No existing test file was modified (`git diff --name-only origin/main -- tests/` shows only the
new tests/unit/test_init_ensures_seam.py).

compiled_state.description:
## Target
`src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — **786 LOC** on origin/main (re-measured at `059d54b725`) against
the 800-LOC hard cap: 14 lines of headroom.

## The concern boundary (derived from the call graph)

`init.py` today carries TWO subsystems with different owners, different lifecycles and no calls
between them:

1. **Host-repo tracker provisioning** (the `init` command proper) — resolve the repo, write
   `.git/info/exclude`, take the 30s mkdir lock, mount-or-create the `tickets` branch worktree,
   the linked-worktree symlink path, the `pending_init_*` predicates, and the CLI entry point.
   Entry points: `init_cli` → `init_core` → `_mount_or_create_branch` / `_init_via_symlink`.

2. **Tickets-branch convergence units** — the check-then-act, idempotent, drift-correcting
   ensure units. `init.py` does **not** call these. Their sole caller is
   `rebar._store.ensures._registry()`, which lazy-imports them by name and dispatches them from
   `run_ensures()`. `ensures.py`'s own module docstring already records the seam verbatim: *"The
   unit implementations live in `rebar._commands.init` (they own the `.gitignore`/
   `.gitattributes` content constants); `run_ensures` lazy-imports them."* That sentence IS the
   architectural boundary — the units live in `init.py` only because they own the two content
   templates, not because init calls them.

The split follows seam 2: extract the **content/config convergence units together with the two
content templates they are the sole readers of**.

## What moves — `src/rebar/_commands/_init_ensures.py` (new, ~215 LOC)
- `_GITIGNORE`, `_GITATTRIBUTES` (the tickets-branch content templates)
- `_gc_config_unit`, `_merge_ours_unit` (git-config convergence)
- `_gitignore_unit`, `_gitattributes_unit`, `_store_compat_unit` (committed-blob convergence)
- a module-local `_git` thin wrapper over the shared `rebar._store.gitutil.run_git_write` seam
  (same two-line form init keeps, carrying its `# raw-git-ok:` marker)

## What deliberately STAYS in `init.py` (~600 LOC), and why
- Everything in subsystem 1.
- `_untrack_runtime_markers_unit` + `_UNTRACK_BATCH`. Two reasons: (a) it is not a *content*
  converger — it has no template and repairs a legacy INDEX state (`git rm --cached`) rather
  than materializing a tickets-branch artifact; (b) **binding**:
  `tests/unit/test_ensures_untrack_markers.py:155` does
  `monkeypatch.setattr(init_mod, "_UNTRACK_BATCH", 3)` and then calls the unit. Moving the unit
  away from the constant would silently stop that patch applying — the test would still pass
  while no longer exercising the multi-batch path. That is a behaviour change, so the unit stays
  with the constant it reads.

## Binding check — BOTH sides, already performed
Serena `find_referencing_symbols` + a plain string `grep` for every moved symbol across
`src/ tests/ docs/ scripts/ .github/`. Findings that constrain the seam:
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:96-100` reaches the units as **module attributes**
  (`init._gc_config_unit`, …). Preserved by re-exporting the moved names from `init.py`, so
  `_registry()` needs no change and `test_ensures_untrack_markers.py:214`'s
  `is`-identity assertion keeps holding.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_ensure_drift_matrix.py:25` does
  `from rebar._commands.init import _GITIGNORE` — preserved by the same re-export.
- Monkeypatches pinned to the `init` module (`run_git`, `_git`, `_git_ok`, `_git_fetch`,
  `_ensure_branch_user_config`, `init_core`, `_UNTRACK_BATCH`) all target symbols that STAY;
  verified that no test patches `init._git` on any path that reaches a moved unit
  (`tests/interfaces/store/test_ensures.py` and `test_ensure_drift_matrix.py` patch only env
  vars, `ensures.write_lock` and `ensures._registry`).
- Prose citations naming `init._gc_config_unit` / `_gitignore_unit` / `_store_compat_unit`
  (`_store/sync.py`, `_store/project_ensures.py`, `docs/adr/0051`, `docs/scale-envelope.md`,
  `docs/migrations.md`, two test docstrings) stay TRUE because of the re-export; the one
  sentence that names the units' *home* — `ensures.py`'s module docstring — is updated to name
  the new module.

## Path-keyed registries checked (lesson from Gerrit 1916)
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — keyed `<path>::<symbol>`; the only `init.py` entry is
  `_mount_or_create_branch` (18), which STAYS, so the move adds no key. Verified by running
  `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` directly and requiring
  `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.
- `tests/scripts/test_cli_seam_clean_heldout.py` `_OWNED_FILES` / `_MARKER_BUDGET` — the new
  module carries zero ambient config reads and zero `# read-via:` markers, so the
  config-ownership gate stays at zero findings for the owned set.
- `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` — the moved `_git` wrapper carries its `# raw-git-ok:`
  reason marker so the raw-git gate stays green.
- `tests/unit/test_init_no_hardcoded_tracker.py` scans `init_mod.__file__`; the moved text
  contains no single-line `.tickets-tracker` literal, so its guarded surface is unchanged.
- `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is NOT touched.

## Method
Behaviour-preserving move only — no logic edits. RED first: a size assertion demonstrating
`init.py` over the target, plus running the existing ensure suites against the new layout;
GREEN by the move. No existing test is modified.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `wc -l < src/rebar/_commands/init.py` reports a value at or below 650 (real headroom, well
      inside the gate's `LIMIT - LIMIT/10` = 720 near-cap band).
- [x] `wc -l < src/rebar/_commands/_init_ensures.py` reports a value of at least 100.
- [x] `_init_ensures.py` defines `_GITIGNORE`, `_GITATTRIBUTES`, `_gc_config_unit`,
      `_merge_ours_unit`, `_gitattributes_unit`, `_gitignore_unit`, `_store_compat_unit`.
- [x] `python -c "from rebar._commands import init; from rebar._store import ensures;
      r = ensures._registry(); assert r['gc-config'] is init._gc_config_unit"` exits 0 — the
      re-export keeps every `init._<name>` citation and the registry wiring resolving.
- [x] `grep -q '_init_ensures' src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` exits 0 — the `ensures.py` module
      docstring names `_init_ensures` as the units' new home, so no stale prose is stranded.
- [x] `git diff --name-only origin/main -- tests/` prints nothing: no existing test is modified.
- [x] `pytest -m "not integration and not external" tests/unit tests/interfaces tests/scripts
      tests/e2e` exits 0 — validated across the WHOLE tree, not one directory.
- [x] `make lint` exits 0.
- [x] `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [x] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0 and reports
      `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.
- [x] `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- .github/module-size-limit.txt` exits 0.
- [x] The commit message NAMES the concern boundary and says why the call graph supports it.
